finalText:
Redis went down at 02:14:07, at `10.0.0.12:6379`, and never came back. Every reconnect attempt after that failed the same way, through attempt 12 at 02:31:26.

Once the cache was gone, the app fell back to hitting the store directly. That triggered cache-miss storms, 5-second timeouts, and a growing request queue, climbing from 52 to over 560 against a max of 500.

The pile-up of stuck requests finally exhausted memory. `worker-2` crashed with an out-of-memory error at 02:31:44, and the whole API went unresponsive and was killed at 02:31:52.

So the trigger was Redis dying, and the crash was 17 minutes of backpressure with no working cache. Fixing this means either getting Redis back reliably or adding a circuit breaker so direct-store reads don't pile up when the cache is down.
